tokens_per_run (subagent_tokens).verdict: Flat. 71.8k mean against 72.2k at 1.11.0 and 68.7k at 1.10.0; the per-prompt deltas (-8k to +15k on single runs) are within the spread iteration 10's three repeats showed for the same prompt. The floor a run pays before doing anything (a refusal that only reads SKILL.md) is ~64k, i.e. about 90% of a typical run, and rose ~2k between iterations 10 and 11 without any skill change, so the skill-controlled share is roughly 5-15k per run. The 1.11.1 wording did what it said (doctor 23/36 -> 0/36, --json-brief 4/36 -> 23/36, tool uses 7.9 -> 7.4) and quality held, so it stays; but further SKILL.md-level token work has nowhere left to go at this measurement precision, and the diet theme closes here.

findings: Iteration 11's claim that agents read gotchas.md/scripts.md was a grep artefact (the file names appear in SKILL.md's own text, which every transcript echoes). Corrected in iteration-11.json, CHANGELOG and the README row.

Tokens per run are dominated by the harness's fixed context; SKILL.md size and preflight calls move the total by a few thousand at most. Measure the skill-controlled share (tokens minus the refusal floor) from now on, and stop optimising SKILL.md for tokens.

--json-brief mixed with plain --json in the same run is common (23 runs used brief, 30 used plain): agents use brief on the writing step and plain --json on probe.py, which has no brief form. Fine as is.
